name: Antique Bronze
lede: Antique bronze is a dull, olive-leaning metallic brown meant to look like very old metal.

sections.title: Imitating age
sections.body:
Paterson defines antique bronze as a bronze colour imitating that of very old objects, and notes that antique gold, antique green and antique red are named the same way [1]. The word antique, in colouring, means the effect of making an object look antique, and is used for brass, bronze and gold [1].

The dictionary also files antique bronze with the metallic colors [2]. It is a finish name, not a pigment [1][2]. It belongs to a small set of finish names that borrow age as a look: new paint made to resemble worn metal [1][2]. Nothing in the books ties it to one pigment or one maker [1][2]. The word antique here describes an intended effect, so the color is defined by what it imitates, not by what it is made of [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #665D1E is a dark olive-gold [3]. Neighbors are [[bronze]], [[antique-brass]], [[olive]] and [[gold]] [3]. A flat screen color can only hint at the shimmer of real metal [3].
